name: Pig Pink
lede: Pig Pink is a warm, moderate pink from the ISCC-NBS color system, closer to a real pig's skin than to the pale cartoon pink the name suggests.

sections.title: Not the cartoon pink
sections.body:
The ISCC-NBS system, published in 1955, files this hue as "moderate purplish pink" in block 250 [1]. Wikipedia's record of the name cites Plochere as an earlier source, and xkcd's 2010 color survey, built from an open web poll of how people name colors, recorded a similar hue independently [1]. In Munsell it reads 7.3RP 6.8/8.7, warmer and a touch more purple than the flat, pale pink often drawn for pigs in illustration [1].

Our library also flags a near-duplicate, Charm Pink, 2.0 CIEDE2000 units away — close enough that the two names are easy to confuse on screen even though they come from separate sources [1]. The nearest color in our own data is [[mauvelous|Mauvelous]], 2.8 units off, with [[pink|Pink]], [[schauss-pink|Schauss Pink]] and [[amaranth-pink|Amaranth Pink]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pig Pink appears in just 5 of our 23,781 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 2, rarer than 82 percent of our named colors [2]. The two usable matches come from paintings dated 1655 and 1908 [2]. In printed English the phrase "pig pink" is a recent coinage, rising fastest and peaking in the 2000s, long after the paintings in our archive were made [2].
